chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Basir from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

"From the completion of fasting is giving the zakat, just as sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is from the completion of the prayer. And whoever fasts and does not pay it (zakat), there is no fast for him if he leaves it deliberately. And whoever prays and does not send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and leaves that deliberately, there is no prayer for him. Indeed, Allah (the Exalted) began with it before the prayer, saying: 'He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself [by paying zakat] and mentions the name of his Lord and prays.'"

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And sending blessings (salat) in the prayer is a sunnah (recommended act) and is not a fard (obligatory duty) that invalidates the prayer if left. Evidence for that is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is paying zakat required for fasting to be valid, and is sending blessings upon the Prophet mandatory in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt tradition links the spiritual perfection of fasting to the purification of wealth through zakat, mirroring how prayer is completed by sending blessings upon the Prophet and his family. While the hadith emphasizes the necessity of these acts for the 'completeness' (tamam) of worship, Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies in his commentary that sending blessings is a confirmed sunnah rather than a fard that invalidates the prayer if omitted. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between acts that perfect worship and those that are strictly obligatory for its validity.
